subject: Post-demo billing scenarios & prefix cache assumptions
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom@clearlens.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo billing scenarios & prefix cache assumptions

Tom — great demo earlier, thanks for the time. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the concrete billing scenarios we discussed and the prefix-cache assumptions that drive the effective $/1M token economics. Attached: a simple worksheet (clearlens_billing_model_v2.xlsx) and a visualization of hit-rate sensitivity (prefix_cache_hitrate_chart.png).

Summary (short):
- Your stated size today: ~100M tokens / month (peak patterns: bursty during ingest windows; ~priority queries with repeated context).
- Target budget range you mentioned on the call: $25k–$75k / month for inference (hosted + any infra).
- Primary ask: a target effective price around $700–$900 per 1M tokens once caching is considered.

Key assumptions I used in the attached worksheet (please confirm):
1) Baseline inference cost (raw model runtime) for the recommended model family: $1,200 per 1M tokens. This is our run-rate estimate for the workload shape you described.
2) Cached-prefix serving cost (serving cached tokens from KV/prefix layer) estimated at $50 per 1M cached tokens (dominated by memory and minimal GPU cycles).
3) Effective cost calculation: effective_cost = (1 - hit_rate)*baseline + hit_rate*cache_cost.

Illustrative scenarios (from the sheet):
- No cache (0% hit): effective = $1,200 / 1M
- 40% prefix-hit: effective = 0.6*$1,200 + 0.4*$50 = $740 / 1M
- 70% prefix-hit: effective = 0.3*$1,200 + 0.7*$50 = $395 / 1M

Notes and caveats:
- Hit-rate depends heavily on prompt standardization: how many tokens are stable prefixes vs dynamic user data. We saw similar customers move from ~15% to ~45% after standardizing prompt templates and caching response prefixes.
- These numbers are illustrative; we’ll run a short trace-based simulation if you can share a 48–72hr sample of anonymized traffic (we only need token lengths and prefix repeat metrics, no PII).

Suggested next steps (action items):
- Tom: confirm the 100M/month estimate and the $25k–$75k monthly budget band; if either is off, flag estimates.
- Tom: if OK, upload 48–72hr sample trace (anonymized) to the Drive link above. Alternative: we can sign an NDA and accept s3 share for the raw logs.
- Marissa / Karthik (internal): we’ll run the simulation and return a 3-slab proposal (pilot, steady-state, committed tier) with expected effective $/1M tokens and recommended cache hit targets.

Thanks — I’ll hold a short follow-up once we get the trace. If you want a quick sensitivity table live, I can share the sheet and walk through numbers tomorrow.

—
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
(415) 555-0198

Attachments: clearlens_billing_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), prefix_cache_hitrate_chart.png (PNG)

From: Tom Ellis <tom@clearlens.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo billing scenarios & prefix cache assumptions

Karthik — thanks for the recap and the clear scenarios. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- The 100M/month is our conservative Q3 estimate for the initial integration (could trend up to ~250M/mo in 6–9 months if the pilot goes well).
- The $25k–$75k budget band was my rough range for inference; procurement would prefer a committed discount if we can get predictable unit economics.
- The $700–$900 target you called out aligns with what our CFO said was acceptable for year-one given expected revenue. Goal would be closer to $600 if we can push hit-rates toward 60%+.

I’m OK to share an anonymized 72hr dump — will scrub PII and push to the Drive link by COB Monday. Two asks before we move to a trace: 
1) Can you include a worked example for a 6-month ramp => shows monthly spend across ramp and the modeled effective $/1M at each month (given a modest improvement in hit-rate over time)?
2) If we go to Dedicated (reserved pool), what delta should we expect vs hosted per-1M effective cost (ballpark)?

If you and Marissa want to sync tomorrow, I’m available 11:00–12:00 PT.

—
Tom
CTO, ClearLens Analytics
tom@clearlens.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Adding a quick internal note and next steps for the model we’ll deliver to Tom: 

Karthik — I pulled the worksheet and tweaked the ramp model per Tom’s ask. Key points I’ll include in the deliverable: 
- 6-month ramp example (assumes 100M -> 250M tokens / month linearly; hit-rate improves from 30% -> 55% through prompt standardization + early cache warmers).
- Monthly spend table + effective $/1M column (see attached updated sheet in Drive).
- Dedicated vs Hosted delta: rough rule-of-thumb we can give now is ~15–25% lower effective cost at steady-state on Dedicated for predictable, high-utilization customers (this depends on model family & quantization). I flagged a follow-up with Pricing to validate exact slabs for CL-8921 if they commit to a 12-month reserved capacity.

Action items I’ll own this week:
- Run trace-based simulation once Tom drops the 72hr anonymized dump.
- Produce the 6-month ramp table + two commercial options: Pilot (month-to-month, higher per-1M) and Committed (12-mo, stronger slabs & a cache-SLA).
- Draft the initial pricing play with three recommended hit-rate targets (30%, 50%, 70%) and the expected effective $/1M for each.

Karthik — will you join the 11:00–12:00 PT sync if Tom confirms? I’ll include a short deck and the updated spreadsheet.
